function.mechanism: Hygroscopic polyol that retains water in foods, helps maintain softness/texture, and acts as a solvent carrier for flavors and colors.

adi.basis: EFSA re-evaluation (2017) concluded no need for a numerical ADI (ADI not specified); 2022 follow-up maintained no general safety concern under assessed uses.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA 2017 found no concern for genotoxicity/carcinogenicity and no need for a numerical ADI; EFSA 2022 follow-up found no safety concern for most groups but could not fully exclude concern for high-percentile toddlers/children due to uncertainties.

adi.basis: NOT SPECIFIED (listed as ADI not specified (1976) in the JECFA database entry).

concerns.summary: Recent human volunteer data indicate gut microbiota can convert dietary glycerol to acrolein, with higher urinary acrolein biomarkers after high-glycerol meals.
EFSA follow-up identified uncertainty for toddlers/children at high-percentile exposure estimates under conservative assumptions.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017 reported no concern for genotoxicity and carcinogenicity and no need for a numerical ADI.
JECFA lists ADI as not specified.
FDA/eCFR lists glycerin as GRAS when used in accordance with GMP.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI exists, but EFSA 2022 noted that no concern could not be fully excluded for toddlers and children at high-percentile refined exposure because of residual uncertainty.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory bodies (EFSA, FDA, JECFA) remain broadly permissive, and glycerol is an endogenous/naturally occurring metabolite. However, EFSA highlighted uncertainty for high-end child exposure scenarios and recent mechanistic human data suggest potential microbiome-mediated acrolein formation after high-glycerol intake.
key_factors: EFSA 2017: no need for numerical ADI
EFSA 2022 follow-up: no concern for most groups; uncertainty for high-end toddlers/children
FDA GRAS status under 21 CFR 182.1320 with GMP condition
No specific IARC classification entry identified for glycerol
